title: Slimline Tool Provenance & Prefetch — PRD rough
content:
TLDR:
This PRD sketches a compact surface for two related problems that come up in interactive hosted calls: (1) identifying and propagating tool provenance/intent to downstream toollets and clients without bloating streaming payloads; (2) a small prefetch manifest that allows SDKs and client runtimes to request tiny warm-ups (kv, token-prefix cache, tool-resolves) before a full call so latency-sensitive UX paths stay under SLO. The goal is to improve median and P95 latency for tool-heavy incremental streams while keeping SDK ergonomics simple and avoiding coupling to a heavyweight orchestration layer.

Goals (high level):
- Reduce first-byte latency on common tool-calling flows by enabling a lean prefetch hint. Target: 10-30ms median improvement on mobile-like payloads in our latency lab.
- Provide stable, minimal provenance metadata so clients and tool adaptors can make safe decisions (retries, local short-circuit, caching) without full model output parsing.
- Keep streaming wire-format compact and backward-compatible with existing incremental frames.
- Provide clear SDK ergonomics for web/mobile server-side use cases — one small change to the SDK surface.

Non-goals:
- Not a full orchestration language or DSL for complex tool graphs (no DAG runtime).
- Not addressing large-scale model-routing/fallback logic — those remain routing policies in the control plane.
- Not a replacement for full evals or fidelity regression tooling.

User stories:
- As a product engineer embedding a chat widget, I want the client to open a connection and indicate which tool resolutions it already has locally so hosted-api can avoid redundant resolves and speed up first actionable bytes.
- As an SDK engineer, I want a tiny declarative API to request a prefetch so I can warm the kv cache and pre-resolve a particular tool endpoint before sending the main prompt.
- As an SRE, I want provenance metadata on tool resolves so I can attribute tool cost and monitor misrouted tool calls.

Design overview (concepts):
1) Prefetch manifest (optional): a concise inline hint attached to a request. Small JSON with: keys_to_prefetch: [prefix-hash], tool_resolve_hints: [{tool_id, ephemeral_token_hint?}], prewarm_kv: boolean. Prefetch hints are advisory — the server may fulfill them opportunistically.
2) Tool provenance envelope (stream-level header): a compact token describing the origin/intent of a tool call in the stream (2-3 fields): provenance_type (model_action | client_action), declared_tool_id (string), declared_confidence_hint (low|medium|high). This lives in the initial frame and in any subsequent tool-invocation frame.
3) Sparse structured output binding: small typed envelopes that carry minimal structured outputs (e.g., {type: 'action', name: 'lookup', args: {id:..}}) but also attach provenance and optional cache_key. Envelopes are intentionally tiny and designed to be compared/merged by SDKs.

Wire-format considerations (backwards compat):
- The prefetch manifest is an optional field on the initial call payload. When absent, behavior is unchanged.
- The provenance envelope uses short enumerated field names to keep bytes small. Example minimal frame (pseudo):
  - init_frame: {prefetch: {k: ['p1'], tools: ['t-send']}, prov: {t: 'model_action', id: 't-send', c: 'med'}}
- SDKs should ignore unknown fields to preserve forward compatibility.

SDK ergonomics proposal (one tiny API change):
- Add a single optional param to existing createStream/createChat call: prefetch: { kv_prefixes: [string], tool_hints: [{tool_id, auth_hint}], prewarm_kv: boolean }
- Add a single covariant event on stream: onPrefetchStatus(status) where status is one of: accepted | partial | denied | completed. The event is advisory and should not block stream consumption.
- Tool provenance surfaces in the parsed envelope as stream.provenance (immutable).

Examples (pseudo-usage):
- Client (web):
  stream = client.createChat({prompt, prefetch: {kv_prefixes: ['user:123:recent'], tool_hints: [{tool_id: 'calendar', auth_hint: 'maybe'}]}})
  stream.on('prefetch', s => console.log('prefetch', s))
  stream.on('message', msg => handleMessage(msg))

Operational and safety rules:
- Prefetch requests are advisory; server will enforce rate limits per-account. Excessive prefetch activity is counted against quota.
- Tool provenance is not an authorization claim. Tool adapters must still validate auth and permissions server-side. Provenance is for routing, telemetry, and client short-circuiting only.
- Prefetch cannot carry customer PII beyond short keys. We will add a hard limit to key size (e.g., 256 bytes) and sanitize.

Telemetry and metrics to track: (new)
- Prefetch accept rate (per account, per model).
- Time delta between prefetch completion and first actionable token.
- Median/P95 first-action latency for flows with and without prefetch.
- Tool provenance distribution and attribution (how many invocations declared as client_action vs model_action).
- Client-side event counts for onPrefetchStatus: partial/denied patterns.

SLOs and target outcomes:
- Target 95th percentile first-action latency reduction of at least 15% in tool-heavy mobile workloads after enabling prefetch on 30% of calls in the lab.
- Prefetch denial rate under normal usage: <3% (denials due to quotas/permissions).

Privacy and compliance notes:
- We will never send full tool credentials in the prefetch hint. Any tool auth_hint is boolean or ephemeral-nonce that server-side subsystems can exchange for tokens under existing KMS/HSM policies.
- Audit logs must include provenance token for each tool invocation (forensics and billing).

Rollout and experiment plan (4 steps):
1) Lab prototype (2 weeks): server honors prefetch hints in a no-op way (simulate warm caches) and emits telemetry. SDK accepts param but ignores onPrefetchStatus. Validate metrics and bandwidth impact.
2) Canary (1 month): enable prefetch acceptance for 5% of hosted requests for internal teams. Observe latency improvement and denial modes.
3) Beta (2 months): open to public customers with opt-in flag. Monitor SLOs and quota pressure.
4) GA: after 80% of beta calls show stable improvements and no security concerns. Include docs and SDK examples.

Open questions (prioritized):
- How opinionated should the server be about prefetch prioritization? (e.g., always do kv vs prioritize tool resolves) -> default: kv first, tool resolves conditional on client-provided auth_hint.
- Do we need a signed provenance token or fresh JWT for stronger trust? This adds complexity; start with unsigned enumerated fields and add signing later if fraud patterns appear.
- Should provenance feed into routing (e.g., prefer cheaper tool-hosts for client_action) or be telemetry-only at first? Start telemetry-only, add routing hook flag in second phase.

Implementation notes (engineering sketch):
- Minimal API surface: 2 new protobuf-ish fields in stream init + 1 new event. Implementation in server: prefetch worker pool with very short tail-time limit (50ms) that tries to satisfy hints.
- Storage: small prefetch manifest need not be persisted for long — ephemeral in-flight only.
- SDKs: add the param and event; also add a compatibility shim to ignore older servers.

Next steps / owners: (week 0)
- Product: Priya (owner) — finalize field names and docs for SDK teams.
- Infra/Serving: Xiaowen — prototype prefetch worker and telemetry hooks.
- SDK: Liam — implement surface and implement onPrefetchStatus for JS and mobile.
- Security/Legal: Maya — review PII constraints and logging.

Notes to reviewers (quick ask):
- Focus on API simplicity (one small param + one event). If this can make client code simpler in several flows, we should prefer it.
- Raise concerns if prefetch is likely to be gamed for free compute or creates op-ex costs without commensurate benefit.

Acknowledgements: this is intentionally a rough, compact draft. Will follow with a narrow compatibility appendix showing proto names and exact short-field encodings for streaming frames before the engineering sprint planning meeting.
